CHAPTER I

GENERAL PROVISIONS

Article 1

In this Regional Regulation, what is meant by:

1. Region is the City of Magelang.
2. Regional Government is the Mayor and regional apparatus as elements of the Regional Government administration of the City of Magelang.
3. Mayor is the Mayor of Magelang.
4. Regional Apparatus Work Unit hereinafter abbreviated as SKPD is the regional apparatus in the City of Magelang.
5. Woman is an adult human being of female sex and a person recognized by law as a woman.
6. Child is a person who has not reached 18 years of age, including a child in the womb.
7. Child Victim of Violence is a child who receives harsh treatment either physically, psychologically, economically, socially, sexually, and other losses resulting from state policies, acts of violence and or threats of violence within the scope of the household and community.
8. Victim is a woman and child who experiences misery and or suffering either directly or indirectly as a result of violence.
9. Protection is all efforts aimed at providing a sense of security and fulfilling the rights of victims carried out by the family, integrated services, advocates, social institutions, police, prosecutors, courts, or other parties either temporarily or based on court decisions.
10. Protection of women is all activities aimed at providing a sense of security carried out by the police, prosecutors, courts, social institutions, or other parties who know or hear that violence against women will or has occurred.
11. Protection of children is all activities to guarantee and protect children and their rights so that they can live, grow, develop, and participate optimally in accordance with human dignity and dignity, and receive protection from violence and discrimination.
12. Implementation of protection is a series of activities aimed at preventing the occurrence of violence, providing protection and recovery services and social reintegration, coordinating and cooperating, and increasing community participation carried out by the Integrated Service Center.
13. Violence is any act that results in or causes misery and suffering whether physical, sexual, psychological including threats of certain actions, coercion or deprivation of liberty arbitrarily, whether occurring in public or in private life.
14. Violence against women is any act based on gender differences that results in or may result in misery or suffering of women physically, sexually, economically, socially, psychologically, including threats of certain actions, coercion or deprivation of liberty, whether occurring in public or in private life
15. Violence against Children is any act against a child that results in misery or suffering physically, mentally, sexually, psychologically, economic exploitation, socially including neglect and maltreatment that threatens the integrity of the body and degrades the dignity of the child.
16. Domestic violence is any act against a person especially women that results in misery or suffering physically, sexually, psychologically and or domestic neglect including threats to commit acts of coercion or deprivation of liberty unlawfully within the scope of the household.
17. Prevention is a direct effort made by the Regional Government to prevent the occurrence of acts of violence against women and children.
18. Complaint is a notification either in writing or orally by the interested party to the authorized institution, in which the person concerned suffers losses due to the actions of others.
19. Service is immediate activities and actions carried out by Professional personnel in accordance with their respective professions in the form of counseling, therapy and advocacy for the empowerment and recovery of victims of violence.
20. Integrated Service is a series of activities to provide protection for women and children victims of violence carried out jointly by relevant agencies or institutions as a unified implementation, prevention efforts, health services, psychosocial rehabilitation, repatriation, social reintegration, and legal assistance for victims of gender-based violence and children.
21. Integrated Service Center for the Protection of Women and Children hereinafter abbreviated as P2TP2A is an institution providing services to victims of violence, carried out jointly by relevant agencies or institutions as a unified implementation, prevention efforts, health services, psychosocial rehabilitation, repatriation, social reintegration, and legal assistance for victims of gender-based violence and children.
22. Health Service is an effort that includes promotive, preventive, curative and rehabilitative aspects.
23. Spiritual guidance is assistance in the form of services for spiritual strengthening so that sick people can rise to be closer to God so that a sense of calm, security arises, and becomes mentally healthy.
24. Legal assistance is legal services provided by legal companions or advocates to carry out the process of accompanying witnesses and / or victims of violence against women and children.
25. Community is individuals, families, groups, social organizations and/or community organizations.
26. Victim Recovery is all efforts to empower victims of gender-based violence and violence against children to be more empowered, whether physically, psychologically, socially, economically or sexually.
27. Assistance is all actions in the form of counseling, psychological therapy, advocacy, and spiritual guidance, for self-empowerment of victims of gender-based violence and violence against children to resolve the problems faced.
28. Social Reintegration is the process of preparing the community and victims that supports the reunification of victims into the family environment, family substitutes who can provide protection and fulfillment of the needs of victims.
29. Safe House (shelter) is a temporary residence used to provide protection to victims in accordance with the determined operational standards.

I. GENERAL

As we are all aware, protection of children and women victims of violence nowadays requires serious attention, particularly for Magelang City in implementing the Women's Empowerment and Child Protection program, as set forth in the Medium-Term Development Plan of Magelang City for 2011-2015.

This is to provide understanding that every Citizen has the right to obtain security and freedom from all forms of violence, especially within the Household and those who potentially become victims are generally women, as well as acts of violence and exploitation against children.

Therefore, it is expected that particularly women can know and understand various aspects of domestic violence.

As mandated in Law Number 23 of 2004 concerning Elimination of Domestic Violence, it has been stated that all forms of violence, especially violence against Women and Children constitute violations of human rights and crimes against human dignity as well as a form of Discrimination that must be eliminated, so that they must receive protection from the State and or society in order to avoid and be free from violence, threats of torture or treatment that degrades human dignity.

Statistically, cases of violence against women and children in Magelang City are relatively small, this is evidenced in 2011 when Magelang City received the Anugerah Parahita Ekapraya Intermediate Level award from the President of the Republic of Indonesia, this shows that the assessment of Women's Empowerment activities in Magelang City including handling of acts of violence against women and children is relatively successful. However, the possibility of cases that still exist and must be handled will always be given attention.

In relation to this, the Magelang City Government needs to establish a Regional Regulation concerning Provision of Protection for Women and Children Victims of Violence that regulates clearly, firmly, and comprehensively to better understand and know various forms of acts of violence against women and children and where to seek protection.

Article 20

1. In providing protection for victims of violence against women and children, the Regional Government may cooperate with the Government, Provincial Government, other regional governments and other institutions.
2. Cooperation between the Regional Government and the Government includes consultation, coordination, and reporting.
3. Cooperation with other regional governments and other institutions as referred to in paragraph (1) includes coordination, advocacy, referral, repatriation, social reintegration, and development of integrated service systems.

CHAPTER III

SCOPE

Article 4

The scope of protection of women and children victims of violence includes the rights of victims, obligations and authorities of the Regional Government, implementation of protection, reporting, control, guidance, and supervision, community participation and financing.

Article 19

Monitoring and reporting as referred to in Article 12 letter f, includes monitoring, documentation, and reporting of cases of violence against women and children.

CHAPTER VIII

CONTROL, GUIDANCE AND SUPERVISION

Article 23

1. The Mayor implements control, guidance, and supervision of the provision of protection for victims of violence against women and children.
2. Control, guidance, and supervision as referred to in paragraph (1) shall be implemented by the SKPD responsible for women's empowerment and child protection.

CHAPTER VII

REPORTING

Article 22

1. P2TP2A reports prevention, handling and protection activities for women and children victims of violence to the SKPD responsible for women's empowerment.
2. The Head of SKPD responsible for women's empowerment reports prevention, handling and protection activities for women and children victims of violence to the Mayor.
3. The Mayor reports protection of women and children victims of violence to the Governor.
4. Further provisions regarding procedures and mechanisms for reporting as referred to in paragraph (1), paragraph (2), and paragraph (3) shall be regulated by Mayor Regulation.

Article 8

In implementing protection for women and children victims of violence, the Regional Government is assisted by P2TP2A.

CHAPTER X

FINANCING

Article 25

Financing of activities related to the provision of protection for women and children victims of violence may be sourced from:
a. State Revenue and Expenditure Budget;
b. Provincial Regional Revenue and Expenditure Budget;
c. Regional Revenue and Expenditure Budget; and/or
d. other legal and non-binding sources.

In addition to the rights as referred to in Article 5, every victim must:
a. provide truthful information to interested parties;
b. become a witness if it does not endanger oneself and if there is a security guarantee for the victim.

CHAPTER I

GENERAL PROVISIONS

Article 1

In this Regional Regulation, what is meant by:

1. Region is the City of Magelang.
2. Regional Government is the Mayor and regional apparatus as elements of the Regional Government administration of the City of Magelang.
3. Mayor is the Mayor of Magelang.
4. Regional Apparatus Work Unit hereinafter abbreviated as SKPD is the regional apparatus in the City of Magelang.
5. Woman is an adult human being of female sex and a person recognized by law as a woman.
6. Child is a person who has not reached 18 years of age, including a child in the womb.
7. Child Victim of Violence is a child who receives harsh treatment either physically, psychologically, economically, socially, sexually, and other losses resulting from state policies, acts of violence and or threats of violence within the scope of the household and community.
8. Victim is a woman and child who experiences misery and or suffering either directly or indirectly as a result of violence.
9. Protection is all efforts aimed at providing a sense of security and fulfilling the rights of victims carried out by the family, integrated services, advocates, social institutions, police, prosecutors, courts, or other parties either temporarily or based on court decisions.
10. Protection of women is all activities aimed at providing a sense of security carried out by the police, prosecutors, courts, social institutions, or other parties who know or hear that violence against women will or has occurred.
11. Protection of children is all activities to guarantee and protect children and their rights so that they can live, grow, develop, and participate optimally in accordance with human dignity and dignity, and receive protection from violence and discrimination.
12. Implementation of protection is a series of activities aimed at preventing the occurrence of violence, providing protection and recovery services and social reintegration, coordinating and cooperating, and increasing community participation carried out by the Integrated Service Center.
13. Violence is any act that results in or causes misery and suffering whether physical, sexual, psychological including threats of certain actions, coercion or deprivation of liberty arbitrarily, whether occurring in public or in private life.
14. Violence against women is any act based on gender differences that results in or may result in misery or suffering of women physically, sexually, economically, socially, psychologically, including threats of certain actions, coercion or deprivation of liberty, whether occurring in public or in private life
15. Violence against Children is any act against a child that results in misery or suffering physically, mentally, sexually, psychologically, economic exploitation, socially including neglect and maltreatment that threatens the integrity of the body and degrades the dignity of the child.
16. Domestic violence is any act against a person especially women that results in misery or suffering physically, sexually, psychologically and or domestic neglect including threats to commit acts of coercion or deprivation of liberty unlawfully within the scope of the household.
17. Prevention is a direct effort made by the Regional Government to prevent the occurrence of acts of violence against women and children.
18. Complaint is a notification either in writing or orally by the interested party to the authorized institution, in which the person concerned suffers losses due to the actions of others.
19. Service is immediate activities and actions carried out by Professional personnel in accordance with their respective professions in the form of counseling, therapy and advocacy for the empowerment and recovery of victims of violence.
20. Integrated Service is a series of activities to provide protection for women and children victims of violence carried out jointly by relevant agencies or institutions as a unified implementation, prevention efforts, health services, psychosocial rehabilitation, repatriation, social reintegration, and legal assistance for victims of gender-based violence and children.
21. Integrated Service Center for the Protection of Women and Children hereinafter abbreviated as P2TP2A is an institution providing services to victims of violence, carried out jointly by relevant agencies or institutions as a unified implementation, prevention efforts, health services, psychosocial rehabilitation, repatriation, social reintegration, and legal assistance for victims of gender-based violence and children.
22. Health Service is an effort that includes promotive, preventive, curative and rehabilitative aspects.
23. Spiritual guidance is assistance in the form of services for spiritual strengthening so that sick people can rise to be closer to God so that a sense of calm, security arises, and becomes mentally healthy.
24. Legal assistance is legal services provided by legal companions or advocates to carry out the process of accompanying witnesses and / or victims of violence against women and children.
25. Community is individuals, families, groups, social organizations and/or community organizations.
26. Victim Recovery is all efforts to empower victims of gender-based violence and violence against children to be more empowered, whether physically, psychologically, socially, economically or sexually.
27. Assistance is all actions in the form of counseling, psychological therapy, advocacy, and spiritual guidance, for self-empowerment of victims of gender-based violence and violence against children to resolve the problems faced.
28. Social Reintegration is the process of preparing the community and victims that supports the reunification of victims into the family environment, family substitutes who can provide protection and fulfillment of the needs of victims.
29. Safe House (shelter) is a temporary residence used to provide protection to victims in accordance with the determined operational standards.

Article 6

In addition to the rights as referred to in Article 5, every victim must:
a. provide truthful information to interested parties;
b. become a witness if it does not endanger oneself and if there is a security guarantee for the victim.

CHAPTER III

SCOPE

Article 4

The scope of protection of women and children victims of violence includes the rights of victims, obligations and authorities of the Regional Government, implementation of protection, reporting, control, guidance, and supervision, community participation and financing.

I. GENERAL

As we are all aware, protection of children and women victims of violence nowadays requires serious attention, particularly for Magelang City in implementing the Women's Empowerment and Child Protection program, as set forth in the Medium-Term Development Plan of Magelang City for 2011-2015.

This is to provide understanding that every Citizen has the right to obtain security and freedom from all forms of violence, especially within the Household and those who potentially become victims are generally women, as well as acts of violence and exploitation against children.

Therefore, it is expected that particularly women can know and understand various aspects of domestic violence.

As mandated in Law Number 23 of 2004 concerning Elimination of Domestic Violence, it has been stated that all forms of violence, especially violence against Women and Children constitute violations of human rights and crimes against human dignity as well as a form of Discrimination that must be eliminated, so that they must receive protection from the State and or society in order to avoid and be free from violence, threats of torture or treatment that degrades human dignity.

Statistically, cases of violence against women and children in Magelang City are relatively small, this is evidenced in 2011 when Magelang City received the Anugerah Parahita Ekapraya Intermediate Level award from the President of the Republic of Indonesia, this shows that the assessment of Women's Empowerment activities in Magelang City including handling of acts of violence against women and children is relatively successful. However, the possibility of cases that still exist and must be handled will always be given attention.

In relation to this, the Magelang City Government needs to establish a Regional Regulation concerning Provision of Protection for Women and Children Victims of Violence that regulates clearly, firmly, and comprehensively to better understand and know various forms of acts of violence against women and children and where to seek protection.

GENERAL PROVISIONS

Article 1

In this Regional Regulation, what is meant by:

1. Region is the City of Magelang.
2. Regional Government is the Mayor and regional apparatus as elements of the Regional Government administration of the City of Magelang.
3. Mayor is the Mayor of Magelang.
4. Regional Apparatus Work Unit hereinafter abbreviated as SKPD is the regional apparatus in the City of Magelang.
5. Woman is an adult human being of female sex and a person recognized by law as a woman.
6. Child is a person who has not reached 18 years of age, including a child in the womb.
7. Child Victim of Violence is a child who receives harsh treatment either physically, psychologically, economically, socially, sexually, and other losses resulting from state policies, acts of violence and or threats of violence within the scope of the household and community.
8. Victim is a woman and child who experiences misery and or suffering either directly or indirectly as a result of violence.
9. Protection is all efforts aimed at providing a sense of security and fulfilling the rights of victims carried out by the family, integrated services, advocates, social institutions, police, prosecutors, courts, or other parties either temporarily or based on court decisions.
10. Protection of women is all activities aimed at providing a sense of security carried out by the police, prosecutors, courts, social institutions, or other parties who know or hear that violence against women will or has occurred.
11. Protection of children is all activities to guarantee and protect children and their rights so that they can live, grow, develop, and participate optimally in accordance with human dignity and dignity, and receive protection from violence and discrimination.
12. Implementation of protection is a series of activities aimed at preventing the occurrence of violence, providing protection and recovery services and social reintegration, coordinating and cooperating, and increasing community participation carried out by the Integrated Service Center.
13. Violence is any act that results in or causes misery and suffering whether physical, sexual, psychological including threats of certain actions, coercion or deprivation of liberty arbitrarily, whether occurring in public or in private life.
14. Violence against women is any act based on gender differences that results in or may result in misery or suffering of women physically, sexually, economically, socially, psychologically, including threats of certain actions, coercion or deprivation of liberty, whether occurring in public or in private life
15. Violence against Children is any act against a child that results in misery or suffering physically, mentally, sexually, psychologically, economic exploitation, socially including neglect and maltreatment that threatens the integrity of the body and degrades the dignity of the child.
16. Domestic violence is any act against a person especially women that results in misery or suffering physically, sexually, psychologically and or domestic neglect including threats to commit acts of coercion or deprivation of liberty unlawfully within the scope of the household.
17. Prevention is a direct effort made by the Regional Government to prevent the occurrence of acts of violence against women and children.
18. Complaint is a notification either in writing or orally by the interested party to the authorized institution, in which the person concerned suffers losses due to the actions of others.
19. Service is immediate activities and actions carried out by Professional personnel in accordance with their respective professions in the form of counseling, therapy and advocacy for the empowerment and recovery of victims of violence.
20. Integrated Service is a series of activities to provide protection for women and children victims of violence carried out jointly by relevant agencies or institutions as a unified implementation, prevention efforts, health services, psychosocial rehabilitation, repatriation, social reintegration, and legal assistance for victims of gender-based violence and children.
21. Integrated Service Center for the Protection of Women and Children hereinafter abbreviated as P2TP2A is an institution providing services to victims of violence, carried out jointly by relevant agencies or institutions as a unified implementation, prevention efforts, health services, psychosocial rehabilitation, repatriation, social reintegration, and legal assistance for victims of gender-based violence and children.
22. Health Service is an effort that includes promotive, preventive, curative and rehabilitative aspects.
23. Spiritual guidance is assistance in the form of services for spiritual strengthening so that sick people can rise to be closer to God so that a sense of calm, security arises, and becomes mentally healthy.
24. Legal assistance is legal services provided by legal companions or advocates to carry out the process of accompanying witnesses and / or victims of violence against women and children.
25. Community is individuals, families, groups, social organizations and/or community organizations.
26. Victim Recovery is all efforts to empower victims of gender-based violence and violence against children to be more empowered, whether physically, psychologically, socially, economically or sexually.
27. Assistance is all actions in the form of counseling, psychological therapy, advocacy, and spiritual guidance, for self-empowerment of victims of gender-based violence and violence against children to resolve the problems faced.
28. Social Reintegration is the process of preparing the community and victims that supports the reunification of victims into the family environment, family substitutes who can provide protection and fulfillment of the needs of victims.
29. Safe House (shelter) is a temporary residence used to provide protection to victims in accordance with the determined operational standards.

I. GENERAL

As we are all aware, protection of children and women victims of violence nowadays requires serious attention, particularly for Magelang City in implementing the Women's Empowerment and Child Protection program, as set forth in the Medium-Term Development Plan of Magelang City for 2011-2015.

This is to provide understanding that every Citizen has the right to obtain security and freedom from all forms of violence, especially within the Household and those who potentially become victims are generally women, as well as acts of violence and exploitation against children.

Therefore, it is expected that particularly women can know and understand various aspects of domestic violence.

As mandated in Law Number 23 of 2004 concerning Elimination of Domestic Violence, it has been stated that all forms of violence, especially violence against Women and Children constitute violations of human rights and crimes against human dignity as well as a form of Discrimination that must be eliminated, so that they must receive protection from the State and or society in order to avoid and be free from violence, threats of torture or treatment that degrades human dignity.

Statistically, cases of violence against women and children in Magelang City are relatively small, this is evidenced in 2011 when Magelang City received the Anugerah Parahita Ekapraya Intermediate Level award from the President of the Republic of Indonesia, this shows that the assessment of Women's Empowerment activities in Magelang City including handling of acts of violence against women and children is relatively successful. However, the possibility of cases that still exist and must be handled will always be given attention.

In relation to this, the Magelang City Government needs to establish a Regional Regulation concerning Provision of Protection for Women and Children Victims of Violence that regulates clearly, firmly, and comprehensively to better understand and know various forms of acts of violence against women and children and where to seek protection.

I. GENERAL

As we are all aware, protection of children and women victims of violence nowadays requires serious attention, particularly for Magelang City in implementing the Women's Empowerment and Child Protection program, as set forth in the Medium-Term Development Plan of Magelang City for 2011-2015.

Therefore, it is expected that particularly women can know and understand various aspects of domestic violence.

As mandated in Law Number 23 of 2004 concerning Elimination of Domestic Violence, it has been stated that all forms of violence, especially violence against Women and Children constitute violations of human rights and crimes against human dignity as well as a form of Discrimination that must be eliminated, so that they must receive protection from the State and or society in order to avoid and be free from violence, threats of torture or treatment that degrades human dignity.

Statistically, cases of violence against women and children in Magelang City are relatively small, this is evidenced in 2011 when Magelang City received the Anugerah Parahita Ekapraya Intermediate Level award from the President of the Republic of Indonesia, this shows that the assessment of Women's Empowerment activities in Magelang City including handling of acts of violence against women and children is relatively successful. However, the possibility of cases that still exist and must be handled will always be given attention.

In relation to this, the Magelang City Government needs to establish a Regional Regulation concerning Provision of Protection for Women and Children Victims of Violence that regulates clearly, firmly, and comprehensively to better understand and know various forms of acts of violence against women and children and where to seek protection.

I. GENERAL

As we are all aware, protection of children and women victims of violence nowadays requires serious attention, particularly for Magelang City in implementing the Women's Empowerment and Child Protection program, as set forth in the Medium-Term Development Plan of Magelang City for 2011-2015.

This is to provide understanding that every Citizen has the right to obtain security and freedom from all forms of violence, especially within the Household and those who potentially become victims are generally women, as well as acts of violence and exploitation against children.

Therefore, it is expected that particularly women can know and understand various aspects of domestic violence.

As mandated in Law Number 23 of 2004 concerning Elimination of Domestic Violence, it has been stated that all forms of violence, especially violence against Women and Children constitute violations of human rights and crimes against human dignity as well as a form of Discrimination that must be eliminated, so that they must receive protection from the State and or society in order to avoid and be free from violence, threats of torture or treatment that degrades human dignity.

SUPPLEMENT TO THE REGIONAL GAZETTE OF MAGELANG CITY NUMBER 9

I. GENERAL

As we are all aware, protection of children and women victims of violence nowadays requires serious attention, particularly for Magelang City in implementing the Women's Empowerment and Child Protection program, as set forth in the Medium-Term Development Plan of Magelang City for 2011-2015.

This is to provide understanding that every Citizen has the right to obtain security and freedom from all forms of violence, especially within the Household and those who potentially become victims are generally women, as well as acts of violence and exploitation against children.

Therefore, it is expected that particularly women can know and understand various aspects of domestic violence.

As mandated in Law Number 23 of 2004 concerning Elimination of Domestic Violence, it has been stated that all forms of violence, especially violence against Women and Children constitute violations of human rights and crimes against human dignity as well as a form of Discrimination that must be eliminated, so that they must receive protection from the State and or society in order to avoid and be free from violence, threats of torture or treatment that degrades human dignity.

Statistically, cases of violence against women and children in Magelang City are relatively small, this is evidenced in 2011 when Magelang City received the Anugerah Parahita Ekapraya Intermediate Level award from the President of the Republic of Indonesia, this shows that the assessment of Women's Empowerment activities in Magelang City including handling of acts of violence against women and children is relatively successful. However, the possibility of cases that still exist and must be handled will always be given attention.

In relation to this, the Magelang City Government needs to establish a Regional Regulation concerning Provision of Protection for Women and Children Victims of Violence that regulates clearly, firmly, and comprehensively to better understand and know various forms of acts of violence against women and children and where to seek protection.

CHAPTER I

GENERAL PROVISIONS

Article 1

In this Regional Regulation, what is meant by:

7. Child Victim of Violence is a child who receives harsh treatment either physically, psychologically, economically, socially, sexually, and other losses resulting from state policies, acts of violence and or threats of violence within the scope of the household and community.
8. Victim is a woman and child who experiences misery and or suffering either directly or indirectly as a result of violence.
9. Protection is all efforts aimed at providing a sense of security and fulfilling the rights of victims carried out by the family, integrated services, advocates, social institutions, police, prosecutors, courts, or other parties either temporarily or based on court decisions.
10. Protection of women is all activities aimed at providing a sense of security carried out by the police, prosecutors, courts, social institutions, or other parties who know or hear that violence against women will or has occurred.
11. Protection of children is all activities to guarantee and protect children and their rights so that they can live, grow, develop, and participate optimally in accordance with human dignity and dignity, and receive protection from violence and discrimination.
12. Implementation of protection is a series of activities aimed at preventing the occurrence of violence, providing protection and recovery services and social reintegration, coordinating and cooperating, and increasing community participation carried out by the Integrated Service Center.
13. Violence is any act that results in or causes misery and suffering whether physical, sexual, psychological including threats of certain actions, coercion or deprivation of liberty arbitrarily, whether occurring in public or in private life.
14. Violence against women is any act based on gender differences that results in or may result in misery or suffering of women physically, sexually, economically, socially, psychologically, including threats of certain actions, coercion or deprivation of liberty, whether occurring in public or in private life
15. Violence against Children is any act against a child that results in misery or suffering physically, mentally, sexually, psychologically, economic exploitation, socially including neglect and maltreatment that threatens the integrity of the body and degrades the dignity of the child.
16. Domestic violence is any act against a person especially women that results in misery or suffering physically, sexually, psychologically and or domestic neglect including threats to commit acts of coercion or deprivation of liberty unlawfully within the scope of the household.

20. 25. Community is individuals, families, groups, social organizations and/or community organizations.
26. Victim Recovery is all efforts to empower victims of gender-based violence and violence against children to be more empowered, whether physically, psychologically, socially, economically or sexually.
27. Assistance is all actions in the form of counseling, psychological therapy, advocacy, and spiritual guidance, for self-empowerment of victims of gender-based violence and violence against children to resolve the problems faced.
28. Social Reintegration is the process of preparing the community and victims that supports the reunification of victims into the family environment, family substitutes who can provide protection and fulfillment of the needs of victims.
29. Safe House (shelter) is a temporary residence used to provide protection to victims in accordance with the determined operational standards.

GENERAL PROVISIONS

Article 1

In this Regional Regulation, what is meant by:

1. Region is the City of Magelang.
2. Regional Government is the Mayor and regional apparatus as elements of the Regional Government administration of the City of Magelang.
3. Mayor is the Mayor of Magelang.
4. Regional Apparatus Work Unit hereinafter abbreviated as SKPD is the regional apparatus in the City of Magelang.
5. Woman is an adult human being of female sex and a person recognized by law as a woman.
6. Child is a person who has not reached 18 years of age, including a child in the womb.
7. Child Victim of Violence is a child who receives harsh treatment either physically, psychologically, economically, socially, sexually, and other losses resulting from state policies, acts of violence and or threats of violence within the scope of the household and community.
8. Victim is a woman and child who experiences misery and or suffering either directly or indirectly as a result of violence.
9. Protection is all efforts aimed at providing a sense of security and fulfilling the rights of victims carried out by the family, integrated services, advocates, social institutions, police, prosecutors, courts, or other parties either temporarily or based on court decisions.
10. Protection of women is all activities aimed at providing a sense of security carried out by the police, prosecutors, courts, social institutions, or other parties who know or hear that violence against women will or has occurred.
11. Protection of children is all activities to guarantee and protect children and their rights so that they can live, grow, develop, and participate optimally in accordance with human dignity and dignity, and receive protection from violence and discrimination.
12. Implementation of protection is a series of activities aimed at preventing the occurrence of violence, providing protection and recovery services and social reintegration, coordinating and cooperating, and increasing community participation carried out by the Integrated Service Center.
13. Violence is any act that results in or causes misery and suffering whether physical, sexual, psychological including threats of certain actions, coercion or deprivation of liberty arbitrarily, whether occurring in public or in private life.
14. Violence against women is any act based on gender differences that results in or may result in misery or suffering of women physically, sexually, economically, socially, psychologically, including threats of certain actions, coercion or deprivation of liberty, whether occurring in public or in private life
15. Violence against Children is any act against a child that results in misery or suffering physically, mentally, sexually, psychologically, economic exploitation, socially including neglect and maltreatment that threatens the integrity of the body and degrades the dignity of the child.
16. Domestic violence is any act against a person especially women that results in misery or suffering physically, sexually, psychologically and or domestic neglect including threats to commit acts of coercion or deprivation of liberty unlawfully within the scope of the household.
17. Prevention is a direct effort made by the Regional Government to prevent the occurrence of acts of violence against women and children.
18. Complaint is a notification either in writing or orally by the interested party to the authorized institution, in which the person concerned suffers losses due to the actions of others.
19. Service is immediate activities and actions carried out by Professional personnel in accordance with their respective professions in the form of counseling, therapy and advocacy for the empowerment and recovery of victims of violence.
20. Integrated Service is a series of activities to provide protection for women and children victims of violence carried out jointly by relevant agencies or institutions as a unified implementation, prevention efforts, health services, psychosocial rehabilitation, repatriation, social reintegration, and legal assistance for victims of gender-based violence and children.
21. Integrated Service Center for the Protection of Women and Children hereinafter abbreviated as P2TP2A is an institution providing services to victims of violence, carried out jointly by relevant agencies or institutions as a unified implementation, prevention efforts, health services, psychosocial rehabilitation, repatriation, social reintegration, and legal assistance for victims of gender-based violence and children.
22. Health Service is an effort that includes promotive, preventive, curative and rehabilitative aspects.
23. Spiritual guidance is assistance in the form of services for spiritual strengthening so that sick people can rise to be closer to God so that a sense of calm, security arises, and becomes mentally healthy.
24. Legal assistance is legal services provided by legal companions or advocates to carry out the process of accompanying witnesses and / or victims of violence against women and children.
25. Community is individuals, families, groups, social organizations and/or community organizations.
26. Victim Recovery is all efforts to empower victims of gender-based violence and violence against children to be more empowered, whether physically, psychologically, socially, economically or sexually.
27. Assistance is all actions in the form of counseling, psychological therapy, advocacy, and spiritual guidance, for self-empowerment of victims of gender-based violence and violence against children to resolve the problems faced.
28. Social Reintegration is the process of preparing the community and victims that supports the reunification of victims into the family environment, family substitutes who can provide protection and fulfillment of the needs of victims.
29. Safe House (shelter) is a temporary residence used to provide protection to victims in accordance with the determined operational standards.

REGIONAL REGULATION OF MAGELANG CITY

NUMBER 11 OF 2012

CONCERNING

IMPLEMENTATION OF PROTECTION FOR WOMEN AND CHILDREN VICTIMS OF VIOLENCE

Paragraph 1

Prevention Efforts

I. GENERAL

As we are all aware, protection of children and women victims of violence nowadays requires serious attention, particularly for Magelang City in implementing the Women's Empowerment and Child Protection program, as set forth in the Medium-Term Development Plan of Magelang City for 2011-2015.

This is to provide understanding that every Citizen has the right to obtain security and freedom from all forms of violence, especially within the Household and those who potentially become victims are generally women, as well as acts of violence and exploitation against children.

Therefore, it is expected that particularly women can know and understand various aspects of domestic violence.

As mandated in Law Number 23 of 2004 concerning Elimination of Domestic Violence, it has been stated that all forms of violence, especially violence against Women and Children constitute violations of human rights and crimes against human dignity as well as a form of Discrimination that must be eliminated, so that they must receive protection from the State and or society in order to avoid and be free from violence, threats of torture or treatment that degrades human dignity.

Statistically, cases of violence against women and children in Magelang City are relatively small, this is evidenced in 2011 when Magelang City received the Anugerah Parahita Ekapraya Intermediate Level award from the President of the Republic of Indonesia, this shows that the assessment of Women's Empowerment activities in Magelang City including handling of acts of violence against women and children is relatively successful. However, the possibility of cases that still exist and must be handled will always be given attention.

In relation to this, the Magelang City Government needs to establish a Regional Regulation concerning Provision of Protection for Women and Children Victims of Violence that regulates clearly, firmly, and comprehensively to better understand and know various forms of acts of violence against women and children and where to seek protection.

CHAPTER I

GENERAL PROVISIONS

Article 1

In this Regional Regulation, what is meant by:

1. Region is the City of Magelang.
2. Regional Government is the Mayor and regional apparatus as elements of the Regional Government administration of the City of Magelang.
3. Mayor is the Mayor of Magelang.
4. Regional Apparatus Work Unit hereinafter abbreviated as SKPD is the regional apparatus in the City of Magelang.
5. Woman is an adult human being of female sex and a person recognized by law as a woman.
6. Child is a person who has not reached 18 years of age, including a child in the womb.
7. Child Victim of Violence is a child who receives harsh treatment either physically, psychologically, economically, socially, sexually, and other losses resulting from state policies, acts of violence and or threats of violence within the scope of the household and community.
8. Victim is a woman and child who experiences misery and or suffering either directly or indirectly as a result of violence.
9. Protection is all efforts aimed at providing a sense of security and fulfilling the rights of victims carried out by the family, integrated services, advocates, social institutions, police, prosecutors, courts, or other parties either temporarily or based on court decisions.
10. Protection of women is all activities aimed at providing a sense of security carried out by the police, prosecutors, courts, social institutions, or other parties who know or hear that violence against women will or has occurred.
11. Protection of children is all activities to guarantee and protect children and their rights so that they can live, grow, develop, and participate optimally in accordance with human dignity and dignity, and receive protection from violence and discrimination.
12. Implementation of protection is a series of activities aimed at preventing the occurrence of violence, providing protection and recovery services and social reintegration, coordinating and cooperating, and increasing community participation carried out by the Integrated Service Center.
13. Violence is any act that results in or causes misery and suffering whether physical, sexual, psychological including threats of certain actions, coercion or deprivation of liberty arbitrarily, whether occurring in public or in private life.
14. Violence against women is any act based on gender differences that results in or may result in misery or suffering of women physically, sexually, economically, socially, psychologically, including threats of certain actions, coercion or deprivation of liberty, whether occurring in public or in private life
15. Violence against Children is any act against a child that results in misery or suffering physically, mentally, sexually, psychologically, economic exploitation, socially including neglect and maltreatment that threatens the integrity of the body and degrades the dignity of the child.
16. Domestic violence is any act against a person especially women that results in misery or suffering physically, sexually, psychologically and or domestic neglect including threats to commit acts of coercion or deprivation of liberty unlawfully within the scope of the household.
17. Prevention is a direct effort made by the Regional Government to prevent the occurrence of acts of violence against women and children.
18. Complaint is a notification either in writing or orally by the interested party to the authorized institution, in which the person concerned suffers losses due to the actions of others.
19. Service is immediate activities and actions carried out by Professional personnel in accordance with their respective professions in the form of counseling, therapy and advocacy for the empowerment and recovery of victims of violence.
20. Integrated Service is a series of activities to provide protection for women and children victims of violence carried out jointly by relevant agencies or institutions as a unified implementation, prevention efforts, health services, psychosocial rehabilitation, repatriation, social reintegration, and legal assistance for victims of gender-based violence and children.
21. Integrated Service Center for the Protection of Women and Children hereinafter abbreviated as P2TP2A is an institution providing services to victims of violence, carried out jointly by relevant agencies or institutions as a unified implementation, prevention efforts, health services, psychosocial rehabilitation, repatriation, social reintegration, and legal assistance for victims of gender-based violence and children.
22. Health Service is an effort that includes promotive, preventive, curative and rehabilitative aspects.
23. Spiritual guidance is assistance in the form of services for spiritual strengthening so that sick people can rise to be closer to God so that a sense of calm, security arises, and becomes mentally healthy.
24. Legal assistance is legal services provided by legal companions or advocates to carry out the process of accompanying witnesses and / or victims of violence against women and children.
25. Community is individuals, families, groups, social organizations and/or community organizations.
26. Victim Recovery is all efforts to empower victims of gender-based violence and violence against children to be more empowered, whether physically, psychologically, socially, economically or sexually.
27. Assistance is all actions in the form of counseling, psychological therapy, advocacy, and spiritual guidance, for self-empowerment of victims of gender-based violence and violence against children to resolve the problems faced.
28. Social Reintegration is the process of preparing the community and victims that supports the reunification of victims into the family environment, family substitutes who can provide protection and fulfillment of the needs of victims.
29. Safe House (shelter) is a temporary residence used to provide protection to victims in accordance with the determined operational standards.

4. Further provisions regarding procedures and mechanisms for reporting as referred to in paragraph (1), paragraph (2), and paragraph (3) shall be regulated by Mayor Regulation.

CHAPTER I

GENERAL PROVISIONS

Article 1

In this Regional Regulation, what is meant by:

1. Region is the City of Magelang.
2. Regional Government is the Mayor and regional apparatus as elements of the Regional Government administration of the City of Magelang.
3. Mayor is the Mayor of Magelang.
4. Regional Apparatus Work Unit hereinafter abbreviated as SKPD is the regional apparatus in the City of Magelang.
5. Woman is an adult human being of female sex and a person recognized by law as a woman.
6. Child is a person who has not reached 18 years of age, including a child in the womb.
7. Child Victim of Violence is a child who receives harsh treatment either physically, psychologically, economically, socially, sexually, and other losses resulting from state policies, acts of violence and or threats of violence within the scope of the household and community.
8. Victim is a woman and child who experiences misery and or suffering either directly or indirectly as a result of violence.
9. Protection is all efforts aimed at providing a sense of security and fulfilling the rights of victims carried out by the family, integrated services, advocates, social institutions, police, prosecutors, courts, or other parties either temporarily or based on court decisions.
10. Protection of women is all activities aimed at providing a sense of security carried out by the police, prosecutors, courts, social institutions, or other parties who know or hear that violence against women will or has occurred.
11. Protection of children is all activities to guarantee and protect children and their rights so that they can live, grow, develop, and participate optimally in accordance with human dignity and dignity, and receive protection from violence and discrimination.
12. Implementation of protection is a series of activities aimed at preventing the occurrence of violence, providing protection and recovery services and social reintegration, coordinating and cooperating, and increasing community participation carried out by the Integrated Service Center.
13. Violence is any act that results in or causes misery and suffering whether physical, sexual, psychological including threats of certain actions, coercion or deprivation of liberty arbitrarily, whether occurring in public or in private life.
14. Violence against women is any act based on gender differences that results in or may result in misery or suffering of women physically, sexually, economically, socially, psychologically, including threats of certain actions, coercion or deprivation of liberty, whether occurring in public or in private life
15. Violence against Children is any act against a child that results in misery or suffering physically, mentally, sexually, psychologically, economic exploitation, socially including neglect and maltreatment that threatens the integrity of the body and degrades the dignity of the child.
16. Domestic violence is any act against a person especially women that results in misery or suffering physically, sexually, psychologically and or domestic neglect including threats to commit acts of coercion or deprivation of liberty unlawfully within the scope of the household.
17. Prevention is a direct effort made by the Regional Government to prevent the occurrence of acts of violence against women and children.
18. Complaint is a notification either in writing or orally by the interested party to the authorized institution, in which the person concerned suffers losses due to the actions of others.
19. Service is immediate activities and actions carried out by Professional personnel in accordance with their respective professions in the form of counseling, therapy and advocacy for the empowerment and recovery of victims of violence.
20. Integrated Service is a series of activities to provide protection for women and children victims of violence carried out jointly by relevant agencies or institutions as a unified implementation, prevention efforts, health services, psychosocial rehabilitation, repatriation, social reintegration, and legal assistance for victims of gender-based violence and children.
21. Integrated Service Center for the Protection of Women and Children hereinafter abbreviated as P2TP2A is an institution providing services to victims of violence, carried out jointly by relevant agencies or institutions as a unified implementation, prevention efforts, health services, psychosocial rehabilitation, repatriation, social reintegration, and legal assistance for victims of gender-based violence and children.
22. Health Service is an effort that includes promotive, preventive, curative and rehabilitative aspects.
23. Spiritual guidance is assistance in the form of services for spiritual strengthening so that sick people can rise to be closer to God so that a sense of calm, security arises, and becomes mentally healthy.
24. Legal assistance is legal services provided by legal companions or advocates to carry out the process of accompanying witnesses and / or victims of violence against women and children.
25. Community is individuals, families, groups, social organizations and/or community organizations.
26. Victim Recovery is all efforts to empower victims of gender-based violence and violence against children to be more empowered, whether physically, psychologically, socially, economically or sexually.
27. Assistance is all actions in the form of counseling, psychological therapy, advocacy, and spiritual guidance, for self-empowerment of victims of gender-based violence and violence against children to resolve the problems faced.
28. Social Reintegration is the process of preparing the community and victims that supports the reunification of victims into the family environment, family substitutes who can provide protection and fulfillment of the needs of victims.
29. Safe House (shelter) is a temporary residence used to provide protection to victims in accordance with the determined operational standards.

I. GENERAL

As we are all aware, protection of children and women victims of violence nowadays requires serious attention, particularly for Magelang City in implementing the Women's Empowerment and Child Protection program, as set forth in the Medium-Term Development Plan of Magelang City for 2011-2015.

This is to provide understanding that every Citizen has the right to obtain security and freedom from all forms of violence, especially within the Household and those who potentially become victims are generally women, as well as acts of violence and exploitation against children.

Therefore, it is expected that particularly women can know and understand various aspects of domestic violence.

As mandated in Law Number 23 of 2004 concerning Elimination of Domestic Violence, it has been stated that all forms of violence, especially violence against Women and Children constitute violations of human rights and crimes against human dignity as well as a form of Discrimination that must be eliminated, so that they must receive protection from the State and or society in order to avoid and be free from violence, threats of torture or treatment that degrades human dignity.

Statistically, cases of violence against women and children in Magelang City are relatively small, this is evidenced in 2011 when Magelang City received the Anugerah Parahita Ekapraya Intermediate Level award from the President of the Republic of Indonesia, this shows that the assessment of Women's Empowerment activities in Magelang City including handling of acts of violence against women and children is relatively successful. However, the possibility of cases that still exist and must be handled will always be given attention.

In relation to this, the Magelang City Government needs to establish a Regional Regulation concerning Provision of Protection for Women and Children Victims of Violence that regulates clearly, firmly, and comprehensively to better understand and know various forms of acts of violence against women and children and where to seek protection.

9. Protection is all efforts aimed at providing a sense of security and fulfilling the rights of victims carried out by the family, integrated services, advocates, social institutions, police, prosecutors, courts, or other parties either temporarily or based on court decisions.

13. Violence is any act that results in or causes misery and suffering whether physical, sexual, psychological including threats of certain actions, coercion or deprivation of liberty arbitrarily, whether occurring in public or in private life.
14. Violence against women is any act based on gender differences that results in or may result in misery or suffering of women physically, sexually, economically, socially, psychologically, including threats of certain actions, coercion or deprivation of liberty, whether occurring in public or in private life

16. Domestic violence is any act against a person especially women that results in misery or suffering physically, sexually, psychologically and or domestic neglect including threats to commit acts of coercion or deprivation of liberty unlawfully within the scope of the household.
17. Prevention is a direct effort made by the Regional Government to prevent the occurrence of acts of violence against women and children.
18. Complaint is a notification either in writing or orally by the interested party to the authorized institution, in which the person concerned suffers losses due to the actions of others.
19. Service is immediate activities and actions carried out by Professional personnel in accordance with their respective professions in the form of counseling, therapy and advocacy for the empowerment and recovery of victims of violence.
20. Integrated Service is a series of activities to provide protection for women and children victims of violence carried out jointly by relevant agencies or institutions as a unified implementation, prevention efforts, health services, psychosocial rehabilitation, repatriation, social reintegration, and legal assistance for victims of gender-based violence and children.

22. Health Service is an effort that includes promotive, preventive, curative and rehabilitative aspects.
23. Spiritual guidance is assistance in the form of services for spiritual strengthening so that sick people can rise to be closer to God so that a sense of calm, security arises, and becomes mentally healthy.

I. GENERAL

As we are all aware, protection of children and women victims of violence nowadays requires serious attention, particularly for Magelang City in implementing the Women's Empowerment and Child Protection program, as set forth in the Medium-Term Development Plan of Magelang City for 2011-2015.

This is to provide understanding that every Citizen has the right to obtain security and freedom from all forms of violence, especially within the Household and those who potentially become victims are generally women, as well as acts of violence and exploitation against children.

Therefore, it is expected that particularly women can know and understand various aspects of domestic violence.

As mandated in Law Number 23 of 2004 concerning Elimination of Domestic Violence, it has been stated that all forms of violence, especially violence against Women and Children constitute violations of human rights and crimes against human dignity as well as a form of Discrimination that must be eliminated, so that they must receive protection from the State and or society in order to avoid and be free from violence, threats of torture or treatment that degrades human dignity.

Statistically, cases of violence against women and children in Magelang City are relatively small, this is evidenced in 2011 when Magelang City received the Anugerah Parahita Ekapraya Intermediate Level award from the President of the Republic of Indonesia, this shows that the assessment of Women's Empowerment activities in Magelang City including handling of acts of violence against women and children is relatively successful. However, the possibility of cases that still exist and must be handled will always be given attention.

In relation to this, the Magelang City Government needs to establish a Regional Regulation concerning Provision of Protection for Women and Children Victims of Violence that regulates clearly, firmly, and comprehensively to better understand and know various forms of acts of violence against women and children and where to seek protection.

9. Protection is all efforts aimed at providing a sense of security and fulfilling the rights of victims carried out by the family, integrated services, advocates, social institutions, police, prosecutors, courts, or other parties either temporarily or based on court decisions.
10. Protection of women is all activities aimed at providing a sense of security carried out by the police, prosecutors, courts, social institutions, or other parties who know or hear that violence against women will or has occurred.
11. Protection of children is all activities to guarantee and protect children and their rights so that they can live, grow, develop, and participate optimally in accordance with human dignity and dignity, and receive protection from violence and discrimination.
12. Implementation of protection is a series of activities aimed at preventing the occurrence of violence, providing protection and recovery services and social reintegration, coordinating and cooperating, and increasing community participation carried out by the Integrated Service Center.
13. Violence is any act that results in or causes misery and suffering whether physical, sexual, psychological including threats of certain actions, coercion or deprivation of liberty arbitrarily, whether occurring in public or in private life.
14. Violence against women is any act based on gender differences that results in or may result in misery or suffering of women physically, sexually, economically, socially, psychologically, including threats of certain actions, coercion or deprivation of liberty, whether occurring in public or in private life
15. Violence against Children is any act against a child that results in misery or suffering physically, mentally, sexually, psychologically, economic exploitation, socially including neglect and maltreatment that threatens the integrity of the body and degrades the dignity of the child.
16. Domestic violence is any act against a person especially women that results in misery or suffering physically, sexually, psychologically and or domestic neglect including threats to commit acts of coercion or deprivation of liberty unlawfully within the scope of the household.
17. Prevention is a direct effort made by the Regional Government to prevent the occurrence of acts of violence against women and children.
18. Complaint is a notification either in writing or orally by the interested party to the authorized institution, in which the person concerned suffers losses due to the actions of others.

20. Integrated Service is a series of activities to provide protection for women and children victims of violence carried out jointly by relevant agencies or institutions as a unified implementation, prevention efforts, health services, psychosocial rehabilitation, repatriation, social reintegration, and legal assistance for victims of gender-based violence and children.
21. Integrated Service Center for the Protection of Women and Children hereinafter abbreviated as P2TP2A is an institution providing services to victims of violence, carried out jointly by relevant agencies or institutions as a unified implementation, prevention efforts, health services, psychosocial rehabilitation, repatriation, social reintegration, and legal assistance for victims of gender-based violence and children.
22. Health Service is an effort that includes promotive, preventive, curative and rehabilitative aspects.
23. Spiritual guidance is assistance in the form of services for spiritual strengthening so that sick people can rise to be closer to God so that a sense of calm, security arises, and becomes mentally healthy.
24. Legal assistance is legal services provided by legal companions or advocates to carry out the process of accompanying witnesses and / or victims of violence against women and children.
25. Community is individuals, families, groups, social organizations and/or community organizations.
26. Victim Recovery is all efforts to empower victims of gender-based violence and violence against children to be more empowered, whether physically, psychologically, socially, economically or sexually.
27. Assistance is all actions in the form of counseling, psychological therapy, advocacy, and spiritual guidance, for self-empowerment of victims of gender-based violence and violence against children to resolve the problems faced.
28. Social Reintegration is the process of preparing the community and victims that supports the reunification of victims into the family environment, family substitutes who can provide protection and fulfillment of the needs of victims.
29. Safe House (shelter) is a temporary residence used to provide protection to victims in accordance with the determined operational standards.

I. GENERAL

As we are all aware, protection of children and women victims of violence nowadays requires serious attention, particularly for Magelang City in implementing the Women's Empowerment and Child Protection program, as set forth in the Medium-Term Development Plan of Magelang City for 2011-2015.

This is to provide understanding that every Citizen has the right to obtain security and freedom from all forms of violence, especially within the Household and those who potentially become victims are generally women, as well as acts of violence and exploitation against children.

Therefore, it is expected that particularly women can know and understand various aspects of domestic violence.

As mandated in Law Number 23 of 2004 concerning Elimination of Domestic Violence, it has been stated that all forms of violence, especially violence against Women and Children constitute violations of human rights and crimes against human dignity as well as a form of Discrimination that must be eliminated, so that they must receive protection from the State and or society in order to avoid and be free from violence, threats of torture or treatment that degrades human dignity.

Statistically, cases of violence against women and children in Magelang City are relatively small, this is evidenced in 2011 when Magelang City received the Anugerah Parahita Ekapraya Intermediate Level award from the President of the Republic of Indonesia, this shows that the assessment of Women's Empowerment activities in Magelang City including handling of acts of violence against women and children is relatively successful. However, the possibility of cases that still exist and must be handled will always be given attention.

In relation to this, the Magelang City Government needs to establish a Regional Regulation concerning Provision of Protection for Women and Children Victims of Violence that regulates clearly, firmly, and comprehensively to better understand and know various forms of acts of violence against women and children and where to seek protection.

I. GENERAL

As we are all aware, protection of children and women victims of violence nowadays requires serious attention, particularly for Magelang City in implementing the Women's Empowerment and Child Protection program, as set forth in the Medium-Term Development Plan of Magelang City for 2011-2015.

This is to provide understanding that every Citizen has the right to obtain security and freedom from all forms of violence, especially within the Household and those who potentially become victims are generally women, as well as acts of violence and exploitation against children.

Therefore, it is expected that particularly women can know and understand various aspects of domestic violence.

As mandated in Law Number 23 of 2004 concerning Elimination of Domestic Violence, it has been stated that all forms of violence, especially violence against Women and Children constitute violations of human rights and crimes against human dignity as well as a form of Discrimination that must be eliminated, so that they must receive protection from the State and or society in order to avoid and be free from violence, threats of torture or treatment that degrades human dignity.

Statistically, cases of violence against women and children in Magelang City are relatively small, this is evidenced in 2011 when Magelang City received the Anugerah Parahita Ekapraya Intermediate Level award from the President of the Republic of Indonesia, this shows that the assessment of Women's Empowerment activities in Magelang City including handling of acts of violence against women and children is relatively successful. However, the possibility of cases that still exist and must be handled will always be given attention.

In relation to this, the Magelang City Government needs to establish a Regional Regulation concerning Provision of Protection for Women and Children Victims of Violence that regulates clearly, firmly, and comprehensively to better understand and know various forms of acts of violence against women and children and where to seek protection.

CHAPTER I

GENERAL PROVISIONS

Article 1

In this Regional Regulation, what is meant by:

1. Region is the City of Magelang.
2. Regional Government is the Mayor and regional apparatus as elements of the Regional Government administration of the City of Magelang.
3. Mayor is the Mayor of Magelang.
4. Regional Apparatus Work Unit hereinafter abbreviated as SKPD is the regional apparatus in the City of Magelang.
5. Woman is an adult human being of female sex and a person recognized by law as a woman.
6. Child is a person who has not reached 18 years of age, including a child in the womb.
7. Child Victim of Violence is a child who receives harsh treatment either physically, psychologically, economically, socially, sexually, and other losses resulting from state policies, acts of violence and or threats of violence within the scope of the household and community.
8. Victim is a woman and child who experiences misery and or suffering either directly or indirectly as a result of violence.
9. Protection is all efforts aimed at providing a sense of security and fulfilling the rights of victims carried out by the family, integrated services, advocates, social institutions, police, prosecutors, courts, or other parties either temporarily or based on court decisions.
10. Protection of women is all activities aimed at providing a sense of security carried out by the police, prosecutors, courts, social institutions, or other parties who know or hear that violence against women will or has occurred.
11. Protection of children is all activities to guarantee and protect children and their rights so that they can live, grow, develop, and participate optimally in accordance with human dignity and dignity, and receive protection from violence and discrimination.
12. Implementation of protection is a series of activities aimed at preventing the occurrence of violence, providing protection and recovery services and social reintegration, coordinating and cooperating, and increasing community participation carried out by the Integrated Service Center.
13. Violence is any act that results in or causes misery and suffering whether physical, sexual, psychological including threats of certain actions, coercion or deprivation of liberty arbitrarily, whether occurring in public or in private life.
14. Violence against women is any act based on gender differences that results in or may result in misery or suffering of women physically, sexually, economically, socially, psychologically, including threats of certain actions, coercion or deprivation of liberty, whether occurring in public or in private life
15. Violence against Children is any act against a child that results in misery or suffering physically, mentally, sexually, psychologically, economic exploitation, socially including neglect and maltreatment that threatens the integrity of the body and degrades the dignity of the child.
16. Domestic violence is any act against a person especially women that results in misery or suffering physically, sexually, psychologically and or domestic neglect including threats to commit acts of coercion or deprivation of liberty unlawfully within the scope of the household.
17. Prevention is a direct effort made by the Regional Government to prevent the occurrence of acts of violence against women and children.
18. Complaint is a notification either in writing or orally by the interested party to the authorized institution, in which the person concerned suffers losses due to the actions of others.
19. Service is immediate activities and actions carried out by Professional personnel in accordance with their respective professions in the form of counseling, therapy and advocacy for the empowerment and recovery of victims of violence.
20. Integrated Service is a series of activities to provide protection for women and children victims of violence carried out jointly by relevant agencies or institutions as a unified implementation, prevention efforts, health services, psychosocial rehabilitation, repatriation, social reintegration, and legal assistance for victims of gender-based violence and children.
21. Integrated Service Center for the Protection of Women and Children hereinafter abbreviated as P2TP2A is an institution providing services to victims of violence, carried out jointly by relevant agencies or institutions as a unified implementation, prevention efforts, health services, psychosocial rehabilitation, repatriation, social reintegration, and legal assistance for victims of gender-based violence and children.
22. Health Service is an effort that includes promotive, preventive, curative and rehabilitative aspects.
23. Spiritual guidance is assistance in the form of services for spiritual strengthening so that sick people can rise to be closer to God so that a sense of calm, security arises, and becomes mentally healthy.
24. Legal assistance is legal services provided by legal companions or advocates to carry out the process of accompanying witnesses and / or victims of violence against women and children.
25. Community is individuals, families, groups, social organizations and/or community organizations.
26. Victim Recovery is all efforts to empower victims of gender-based violence and violence against children to be more empowered, whether physically, psychologically, socially, economically or sexually.
27. Assistance is all actions in the form of counseling, psychological therapy, advocacy, and spiritual guidance, for self-empowerment of victims of gender-based violence and violence against children to resolve the problems faced.
28. Social Reintegration is the process of preparing the community and victims that supports the reunification of victims into the family environment, family substitutes who can provide protection and fulfillment of the needs of victims.
29. Safe House (shelter) is a temporary residence used to provide protection to victims in accordance with the determined operational standards.
